newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia expects accord with Chechens within days.
newsitem.headline: Russia expects accord with Chechens within days.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin could sign a new accord with the head of Chechnya's self-proclaimed government in two or three days, Kremlin Security Council secretary Ivan Rybkin said on Wednesday.

The deal, Russian officials said, would spell out relations between Moscow and its breakaway province of Chechnya in the period up to January 27, when the separatist administration plans elections for a regional leader and parliament.
"It shouldn't drag on, two or three days," Rybkin told Ekho Moskvy radio.
Rybkin stressed, however, that the agreement should not be over-dramatised and said a number of accords on various issues would contribute piecemeal to consolidating peace in the region.

Chechnya, an oil-rich land on the southern edge of the Russian Federation, was devastated in 21 months of fighting between Chechen rebels and Russian troops sent there in December 1994 to crush the region's independence.
Tens of thousands of people, mainly civilians, died in the fighting which ended with a peace deal struck by Moscow with the rebels on August 31.

Chernomyrdin could go to the Caucasus for the signing, Rybkin said. Or Maskhadov, who led the rebel guerrilla army until being appointed government chief by separatist leader Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev, could travel to Moscow.

Rybkin and Chechen separatist representatives agreed on Tuesday to work out a provisional agreement to clarify relations between Moscow and the breakaway region over the next few months and said a draft would soon be ready.

Interfax news agency quoted Rybkin denying a report that the federal authorities would pump one trillion roubles ($180 million) into Chechnya. Rybkin said the region would only start getting cash after the elections.
